lq.ANSWER: Humanistic education is important in professional ethics because it develops the right understanding required for ethical conduct. Without right understanding, professional education may only develop skills for earning, competition or profit. Humanistic education helps a person understand the comprehensive human goal and use professional knowledge for mutual happiness, mutual prosperity and preservation of nature. It develops the competence to live with definite human conduct. A professional with humanistic education will not use technology, management or knowledge for exploitation or harm. Instead, they will use their profession as a meaningful participation in society and nature. Therefore, humanistic education is the entry point for ethical profession and humane society.
